title: The Bridge Balance
summary: Null a Wheatstone bridge, find the current in an unbalanced one and use a meter bridge.
subject: physics
concepts: Galvanometer current in an unbalanced bridge
learningOutcome: The student can find an unknown resistance from the null point of a Wheatstone bridge, find the galvanometer current when it is unbalanced, and use a meter bridge.

levels.title: Find the null
levels.adds: Baseline: at balance P/Q = R/X, so the unknown is X = RQ/P (Section 3.13).
hints: Turn the rheostat until the needle rests at zero.
At that point no current flows through the galvanometer, so B and D are at the same potential.
Use the ratio P/Q = R/X to find X.

levels.title: An unbalanced bridge
levels.adds: More steps: with the bridge out of balance, find the galvanometer current by the junction rule (Example 3.7).
hints: Take C as 0 V and A as the battery voltage.
Write the junction rule at B and at D, to find V_B and V_D.
The current is (V_B − V_D)/G, towards the lower potential. Give it in mA.

levels.title: The meter bridge
levels.adds: Apply it: the unknown and known resistances are in the ratio of the wire lengths at balance (Section 3.13).
hints: Slide the jockey until the needle rests at zero and read the length.
Swapping X and R swaps the ratio of the lengths.

misconceptions: The bridge balance depends on the battery emf
A balanced bridge has equal currents in all four arms
The galvanometer current is zero only when all four resistances are equal
Swapping the known and unknown resistances leaves the balance point unchanged
